Rocco Arena: THE REGISTERS PROVE THE CAUTION RIGHT. Scilla holds at least TWO different Rocco Arena born three years apart: act 60 of 1858, son of SANTO Arena and Giovanna Gioffre, and act 228 of 1861, son of FRANCESCO ANTONIO Arena and Serafina Arlotta. The Ellis Island index adds four more Rocco Arena of Scilla, born about 1861, 1896, 1897 and 1898. The same town in the same years also produced a Rocco Arlotta, a Rocco Donato, a Rocco Polistena, a Rocco Costa and a Rocco Ciccone. Merging four tree records called Rocco Arena would have been a coin toss.
Giovanni Arena: At least THREE distinct men. The Giovanni Arena of act 230 of 1892, a pescatore of Via Grotte, born about 1859 and NOT found in any Scilla birth register for 1857-1860. The Giovanni Arena of act 1 of 1854, son of Antonio and Rosa Arlotta. And an adult Giovanni Arena married to Maddalena Longordo, fathering Filippo in 1857 and Domenico in 1860 -- so born in the 1830s. Three Giovanni Arena in one small town inside forty years.
Domenico Arena: The best single example in the archive of why a name is not a person: ORAZIO ARENA AND GIOVANNA ZIRILLI NAMED TWO OF THEIR OWN SONS DOMENICO -- act 180 of 1856 and act 46 of 1859. The first child died and the name was given again, which was ordinary practice. One couple, one name, two people. A records-matcher would merge them without hesitating.
Filippo Arena: Two in the direct line alone, a grandfather and a grandson: Filippo Arena the marinaro, married to Domenica Costa by 1817, and Filippo Arena born 14 February 1852, Rocco's eldest brother, named for him. The custom that produces this pattern -- first son takes his father's father's name -- guarantees the collision every second generation.
Serafina Arlotta: Rocco Arena's mother, born about 1830, and his daughter SERAFINA ARENA born in New York in 1898 and dead at seventeen months. Not the same surname, but the same given name deliberately repeated across three generations and two continents -- which is how the archive knew to look.
Salvatore Mazza: Four records in the export. The archive has separately documented a Salvatore Mazza born 5 January 1873 at Piedimonte Etneo who died at Catania in 1929, and a Salvatore Mazza born at Briatico in 1948 who sailed to Fremantle as a small child. Seventy-five years and two provinces apart.
